summary.text: Marsupials are a group of mammals whose young are born in a relatively undeveloped state and nurtured in a pouch on the mother's abdomen.
They are native to Australasia, Wallacea and the Americas, and close to 70% of the 334 living species are on the Australian continent.
Kangaroos, koalas, opossums, Tasmanian devils and wombats are marsupials, and their reproductive organs differ from placentals because the tract is doubled.

facts.label: Share in Australia
facts.value: Close to 70% on the Australian continent

facts.label: North American species
facts.value: Only the Virginia opossum, north of Mexico

items.prompt: A newborn kangaroo is tiny and far from fully formed. Why is this not a problem?

options.label: It finishes developing inside an egg after birth
It keeps developing in a pouch on its mother's abdomen
It is born fully formed but only looks small
It is raised in a nest until it is big enough

items.explain: Marsupial young are born in a relatively undeveloped state and nurtured within a pouch on the mother's abdomen.

items.prompt: Scientists compare pouches across marsupial species and find the openings point in different directions. What best explains this?

options.label: Openings face toward the continent where the species lives
Opening direction depends on how many teats the female has
Every pouch opens forward and slowly turns as the young grow
Layout varies with how each animal moves, to protect the young

items.explain: Kangaroos that hop have a front opening, while many animals that walk or climb on all fours open at the back; the arrangement is variable to give the offspring maximum protection.

items.prompt: Epipubic bones are found in male marsupials and in species without a pouch. What does this suggest about their original job?

options.label: They probably did not serve reproduction but helped move the hind limbs
They were first used to hold the pouch closed
They first helped females carry two young at once
They were first used to protect the males' reproductive organs

items.explain: Because the bones occur in males and pouchless species, they are believed to have first helped the muscles move the hind limbs.

items.prompt: A wildlife officer in Ohio is called about a wild marsupial. Given where marsupials live, which species is it?

options.label: Red kangaroo
Tasmanian devil
Virginia opossum
Long-tailed planigale

items.explain: A single species, the Virginia opossum, lives in North America north of Mexico.

items.prompt: Two unrelated animals on different continents look alike, and one of them is a marsupial. Which explanation fits?

options.label: The marsupial is really a placental in disguise
Convergent evolution made the marsupial resemble the placental
Marsupials recently evolved from placentals
Both animals share a single pouch-bearing parent species

items.explain: Some marsupials resemble placentals and are examples of convergent evolution, even though the two groups split 125 to 160 million years ago.

items.prompt: A vet examines a female marsupial's reproductive anatomy. Which finding is expected?

options.label: Two uteri and two vaginas
One fused uterus, as in placentals
Two uteri but a single vagina
No uterus at all, with young held only in the pouch

items.explain: In marsupials the reproductive tract is doubled: females have two uteri and two vaginas.
